transcript.content: Hello, what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because I keep blowing up at people over basically nothing. Um, for example, I yelled at one of my employees the other day just for putting stock on the wrong shelf. And afterward I was actually shaking, because... that is just not how I usually treat people. I need to figure out what's going on.
Have you had any distinct periods of several days when you felt unusually elevated or persistently irritable compared with your usual self?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. I mean, lately I've been irritable, like I said, but it's not like a period of days where I'm just... up, or constantly on edge for no reason. It's more just these sudden outbursts when something goes wrong. But no, no distinct periods like you're describing.
Have you ever experienced or witnessed a traumatic event that involved serious injury, sexual violence, or a threat to your life?

Yes, um... I was in a fire recently. It was my kitchen. So, yes, it was definitely a threat to my life. And honestly, the fire keeps jumping into my head out of nowhere now. Like, I’ll just pick up a pan, or even be at work opening a spreadsheet, and suddenly I’m right back there. I can smell the smoke and see the kitchen fill up with it before I can even stop it.
How long ago did the fire happen?
It was about two weeks ago. Um, it happened during our first weekend working on the house. So, yeah, all of this has been going on for about two weeks now, ever since then.
Did these sudden angry outbursts begin only after the fire, or were they happening before it?

They definitely started after the fire. That's actually why I'm here. I keep blowing up at people over absolutely nothing. Like, just the other day, I yelled at one of my employees because they put some stock on the wrong shelf. I was practically shaking afterward because... well, that is just not how I usually treat people. I've never been like this before the fire.
Since the fire, have you been unusually jumpy or easily startled?

Yes, absolutely. Like, at work... if a store alarm beeps, or if someone drops a pallet jack with a bang behind me, I jump so hard I almost drop whatever I’m holding. And it's not just a quick flinch. My heart just keeps pounding in my chest long after everyone else has moved on and gone back to what they were doing.
Since the fire, have you deliberately avoided anything that reminds you of it?

Yes, I have. I've been avoiding the house completely. I just... I can't go back there. And it's other things, too, like the mortgage folder, and even the herbs on my patio. It seems like anything tied to that day just makes my chest tighten up. I just can't make myself go near any of it.
Since the fire, have you felt detached from yourself or as though the world around you were unreal?

Yes, actually. Sometimes when I’m walking through the store at work, it... it feels like I’m watching myself from a few feet away. It's like the aisles and the customers are all there, but they don't seem quite real. I'm just kind of moving through them on automatic.
